text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn decided Wednesday to relieve Minister of Agriculture Laszlo Lakos of his post effective December 15. @

- President Bill Clinton addressed a letter to Prime Minister Gyula Horn on Wednesday praising Hungary's participation in the IFOR mission and reconfirming his invitation to prime minister Gyula Horn to attend the SouthEast European Cooperative Initiatiye.

- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs confirmed Wednesday to Parliament's foreign affairs committee that negotiations aimed at reaching an out-of-court settlement with Slovakia regarding the hydroelectric power plant at Gabcikovo have so far yielded no tangible results. @
- Parliament began debate Wednesday of a bill on the 1997 budget of the social insurance sector planning a HUF 12-13 billion deficit.

- The Prosecutor General's Office filed a suit with the Metropolitan Court Wednesday, seeking annulment of the contract concluded between the State Privatisation and Holding Co. and lawyer Marta Tocsik.
- Laszlo Sandor, president of the National Federation of Hungarian Trade Unions is to resign his concurrent post as president of the Health Insurance Authority. @

- GDP stagnated in the first half of 1996, while a slight growth can be projected for the second half; the annual increase is not expected to exceed 0.5 percent, a study by Economic Research Co. and Postabank reveals.
- The spate of armed assaults in Budapest continued Tuesday evening when a businessman was attacked by a gunman.
MAGYAR HIRLAP

- Interior Minister Gabor Kuncze and Minister of Justice Pal Vastagh will represent Hungary at a summit meeting of interior and justice ministers of the European Union and associate countries in Brussels today. @
- The Constitutional Court Wednesday struck down proposals aimed at cancelling the act relating to reductions in the number of hospital beds.
- President Arpad Goncz Wednesday relieved Gyorgy Szabo of his post as welfare minister.
- A new managing director has been appointed to the British American Tobacco-owned Pecsi Dohanygyar in the person of David Grime.
- The insurance firm Colonia Biztosito is expected to close 1996 with premium revenues of HUF 6-6.2 billion. @
- NABI North American Vehicle Ltd and its wholly American-owned subsidiary North American Bus Industries Inc. have won a tender for the supply of buses to Phoenix, Arizona.
- The State Privatisation and Holding Co. is to publish a public tender for the purchase of a 90 percent stake of HUF 1.591 billion face value in aluminum producer Ajkai Aluminiumipari Kft.
NEPSZABADSAG
- A Socialist "platform" was formed within the Socialist Party in Parliament Tuesday afternoon.
VILAGGAZDASAG @

- The cabinet is expected to review the criteria for early retirement and the management of various state funds and look into reports on experiences gained from answers provided to the recent European Commission economic questionnaire.
- Parliament has passed the amended main figures of next year's central budget.
